newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican drug kingpin cleared in disco slayings.
newsitem.headline: Mexican drug kingpin cleared in disco slayings.

text.p: One of Mexico's top alleged drug barons has won a break from the Mexican justice system after he was cleared of a 1992 mafia-style mass killing in a beachside discoteque, officials said on Friday.
Judge Jorge Luis Solis Aranda, told Reuters he had found Hector "The Blond" Palma not guilty of carrying out the killing in the disco in the Pacific resort of Puerto Vallarta that killed five people.
Palma was also absolved of attempting to kill rival drug kingpins, the Arellano Felix brothers, during the hit.
"There is not a shred of concrete proof that suggests Mr. Palma was responsible," the judge said.

The decision on Thursday was the latest in a string of courtroom victories for Palma, who was being held in a maximum-security prison outside Guadalajara in western Mexico, accused by the government of heading the so-called Sinaloa cartel in northern Mexico.

The government has expressed outrage over lenient sentences given to Palma in the past, but did not immediately react to the lastest verdict, saying it had not yet been officially notified of the judge's decision.
Earlier this month, the attorney general's office threatened to launch an investigation of a judge in Guadalajara who slashed Palma's sentence for a weapons conviction to 2-1/2 years from six years.
In January he was cleared of some drug charges, which prosecutors also sought to appeal.
Palma was caught by accident in 1995 when his plane crashed in western Mexico. He still faces charges in three Mexican states for murder, kidnapping and drug-related offences.

The judges' rulings in the various cases against him have been considered major setbacks for the Mexican government, which has sought to reaffirm its drug-fighting credentials in the face of stiff criticism from the United States Congress.
